OpenConnect for Mac/ macOS
EN/RU

Install OpenConnect for Mac.
Make your first connection.

OpenConnect for Mac connects your Mac to your organization’s AnyConnect-compatible VPN gateway. You need macOS 14.4 or newer and access to that gateway.

The command is ocmac; profiles use .ocmac. The installer migrates existing profiles and settings and preserves original user files. System setup stops the previous VPN session.

Have a file from a teammate? Go to installation with a configured profile. It already contains the gateway, networks and DNS settings.

Install with one command

Open Terminal and paste this line:

/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ValeraGin/openconnect-for-mac/main/install.sh)"

The command downloads the installer from GitHub. It checks Git and Swift, offers missing Apple tools and Homebrew, builds OpenConnect for Mac, sets up its system helper and launch at login, then opens the app.

If the Apple tools installation window appears, finish installing there: the script waits for it. The system helper needs your Mac administrator password. Run the line as your regular user. Building may take a few minutes.

Have a profile from a teammate?

After installation, just open the file, enter your username and connect. You do not need to rename the file or edit a path in a command.

If OpenConnect for Mac is not installed yet, open Terminal and run one command:

/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ValeraGin/openconnect-for-mac/main/install.sh)" -- --language en
  1. Double-click the .ocmac file you received. Save it in any convenient folder. You can also choose Open profile… in the app or in Profiles settings.
  2. Enter your own work username. The short window already shows your VPN name and address. Networks, DNS and embedded CSD come from the file.
  3. Choose Connect. Your username is saved automatically. If system setup is needed, the app opens Terminal: enter your Mac administrator password and wait for setup to finish. Connection then continues.

Opening a profile does not run its scripts or connect the VPN. If it contains CSD or custom commands, connect only if you trust the sender.

First connection

Complete your organization’s sign-in with your password and second factor. Once connected, check a work resource and an ordinary public website. Networks and pause are available from the OpenConnect for Mac menu bar icon.

If the installer has already imported a profile without a username, the username window opens automatically. Choose All settings… to change other options. In the editor, Save profile saves the configuration; the button next to the password saves only the password.

For Cisco XML with several servers, choose the profile you need in the new window. Manual configuration and work resource checks remain available in Settings → General → Setup wizard and access check….

Choose English, Russian or System default in Settings → General → Interface language.

The author has verified macOS 26 on Apple Silicon. A clean installation and first sign-in on another Mac have not yet been verified. Sign-in and device checks depend on your organization.

Tell us how your gateway worked: gateway type, sign-in method and result are enough. Do not include corporate addresses or sign-in details.

If the connection fails

ocmac doctor
ocmac status

The app also has a diagnostics and logs window. Start with any failed checks; confirm your gateway, group and authentication requirements with your administrator. Detailed troubleshooting (Russian) covers common failures. Before opening a public issue, remove gateway details, account names, cookies and tokens from any logs you share.

Update

brew upgrade openconnect-for-mac
ocmac app stop
ocmac app start
ocmac doctor

If the release notes or diagnostics report an outdated helper, run sudo ocmac install again. Updates are not installed automatically.

Share a configured profile with a teammate

One .ocmac file brings together the gateway, networks, DNS zones and SSO form rules. New teammates can start with settings you have already checked.

ocmac export main team.ocmac

Here, main is the name of your configured profile. Before sharing, open the file: replace your personal User value, review KeePassXC and CSD wrapper paths, and check any custom commands. Export does not retrieve passwords or TOTP secrets from your credential store; you must review the contents of your own commands and rules. Share work settings within your team.

If CSD is required, open the profile editor’s advanced settings and choose Embed CSD script… before exporting. Export preserves the script inside the file.

Send your teammate team.ocmac and the link to installation with a configured profile. After installation, they double-click the file, enter their own username and choose Connect.

Remove the app and system helper

Keep this order: OpenConnect for Mac must still be installed to remove its system components.

sudo ocmac uninstall
brew uninstall openconnect-for-mac

The first command disconnects OpenConnect for Mac, removes its routes and DNS settings, stops its agents, and removes the helper and its sudoers rule. The second removes the Homebrew package.

Profiles, local logs and state, saved WebKit sign-in data and Keychain credentials remain. These commands are not a full personal-data wipe. Review the full cleanup instructions (Russian) before deleting remaining data. KeePassXC entries are managed separately.
